title: Cross-Ecosystem Vulnerability Analysis for Python Applications
abstract: arXiv:2603.18693v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Python packages often bundle third-party native libraries (e.g., OpenSSL), a practice known as vendoring. Identifying vulnerabilities in these libraries is challenging because current scanners either ignore vendored libraries, causing false negatives, or ignore their origin, causing false positives by missing security fixes backported by OS distributions.   We show that accurate cross-ecosystem vulnerability analysis requires the exact provenance of each vendored binary: its upstream project and version, and, when applicable, the specific OS package and version. We recover provenance deterministically using two complementary techniques. For binaries copied from OS packages, Python packaging tools rewrite metadata but leave executable code unchanged. translated_title: 面向Python应用程序的跨生态系统漏洞分析
translated_abstract: Python包经常捆绑第三方原生库（例如OpenSSL），这种做法被称为“供应商化”（vendoring）。识别这些库中的漏洞具有挑战性，因为当前的扫描器要么忽略被供应商化的库，导致漏报（假阴性）；要么忽略其来源，由于遗漏了操作系统发行版向后移植的安全修复而导致误报（假阳性）。我们证明了准确的跨生态系统漏洞分析需要每个被供应商化的二进制文件的精确来源：其上游项目和版本，以及在适用情况下的特定操作系统包及其版本。我们使用两种互补的技术确定性地恢复来源。对于从操作系统包复制的二进制文件，Python打包工具会重写元数据但保持可执行代码不变，我们对这些代码进行哈希，并将其与历史操作系统包工件进行匹配。对于从源代码构建的库，我们生成针对每个库的动态分析规则来提取版本信息
tldr: 该论文提出通过两种互补的确定性技术精确恢复Python包中捆绑原生库的来源信息（上游项目、版本及操作系统包），从而解决现有扫描器在跨生态系统漏洞分析中漏报和误报的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes two complementary deterministic techniques to precisely recover the provenance (upstream project, version, and OS package) of native libraries vendored in Python packages, addressing the false negatives and false positives of existing cross-ecosystem vulnerability scanners.
